purpose: Checkpoint deterministic 208-state raw-search coverage and ingest substantive methods surfaced specifically by the forced gap-closure pass, including drone payload vibration control, induced quantum coherence, superconducting-normal interfaces and hardware-to-host input injection security.

source_ingestion_policy.rule: Every substantive unique publication, dataset, advisory, standard, method, software resource, operational precedent, commercial signal or information item receives a Worldshepherd use when it materially improves any capability, or an explicit negative-control role.
source_ingestion_policy.duplicates: Publisher mirrors, research-portal copies, repeated NVD/vendor records and alternate bibliographic pages for the same underlying item are provenance aliases and are not independent evidence.
source_ingestion_policy.search_noise: Coverage completion, DOI components, classification codes and CVE identifiers may be useful to Worldshepherd but have zero automatic Glob evidence; only independently verified physical quantities/relations are promoted through the evidence gates.

sources.title: Residual vibration control of artificial pollination sprayer for onboard drones
sources.authority: Japan Society of Mechanical Engineers / Mechanical Engineering Letters
sources.note: Use gimbal payload residual-vibration behavior, reference tracking and control-system redesign as an aerial-payload dynamics/control benchmark. 00031 is DOI/article metadata.

sources.title: Induced coherence with and without induced emission
sources.note: Use path-indistinguishability and induced-emission/coherence relations as a quantum-optics modeling reference. 00314 is the DOI/PII component.

sources.title: Applications of Superconductor–Normal Metal Interfaces
sources.authority: Journal of Low Temperature Physics / Springer Nature
sources.note: Use NIS/SNS/SNIS thermometry, refrigeration, quasiparticle trapping and quantum-circuit interface methods as low-temperature device/measurement references. 03144 is DOI metadata.

sources.title: CVE-2026-25933 — Arduino App Lab hardware metadata command injection
sources.note: Use as a hardware-to-host trust-boundary case: device-supplied Serial/Address metadata containing shell metacharacters could execute commands before version 0.4.0. 25933 is the CVE identifier and is unrelated to ISO/WD 25933 or QPL-25933.

information_updates.finding: The new deterministic analyzer reports explicit raw-search observation coverage for all 208 unique states in the union of the 31542, 13524 and 14523 permutation families after reservoir 30. Coverage classes include physical carry-forward, gated physical, metadata/incidental hits and revisable no-hits.
information_updates.claims_boundary: 208/208 observation coverage is a completeness property of the search ledger, not evidence of statistical anomaly or physical causation.

information_updates.finding: CVE-2026-25933 shows that even device identity metadata (serial/address fields) must be treated as untrusted input when sensor/hardware discovery can reach shell or process-spawning paths.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Generalized security lesson; no claim is made that current Worldshepherd hardware enumeration uses Arduino App Lab.

information_updates.finding: Forcing explicit coverage of previously unobserved states surfaced useful non-Glob work in drone control, quantum coherence and cryogenic device engineering. Completeness gating therefore improves Worldshepherd knowledge capture even when most new numerical occurrences remain nonphysical controls.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Utility gain does not increase Glob evidence weight.

Continue same-system topology and relational verification independently for physical P1/P2 candidates, especially W II and Sr I, without allowing metadata-density to influence promotion.
Maintain fixed tolerance and experiment-wide multiple-testing/false-discovery controls across all target states, datasets, unit families and relational motifs.
